title: Effects of Generative AI-Assisted Media Literacy Instruction on Learning Achievement and Cognitive Load among Elementary School Students
venue: International Journal of Information and Education Technology
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a generative AI chatbot can improve elementary students’ media literacy learning, specifically their ability to detect fake news, while also reducing cognitive load and improving technology acceptance. The authors frame the study around a practical problem: upper elementary students often struggle with online information evaluation because of limited reading comprehension and search skills, which can make traditional fact-checking instruction cognitively demanding.

The intervention embedded Microsoft Copilot into media literacy instruction as a student-facing learning support tool. In the experimental condition, students used natural-language interaction with the chatbot to verify news content, whereas the control group used the Taiwan FactCheck Center website plus conventional Google search strategies. The study used a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design with 56 fifth- and sixth-grade students from one elementary school in Pingtung County, Taiwan, and the same teacher taught both groups. Instruction lasted 120 minutes and focused on fake news detection.

Results showed that the AI-supported group significantly outperformed the control group on the posttest for fake news recognition, even after controlling for pretest scores. The experimental group also reported slightly lower cognitive load, but the differences were not statistically significant. Students reported high perceived usefulness and ease of use for the chatbot. The authors conclude that generative AI chatbots can be effective and acceptable supports for elementary media literacy instruction, while noting that stronger scaffolding and longer-term studies are needed to determine whether the benefits extend beyond novelty effects and short-term gains.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI chatbot system used for natural-language question answering and interactive assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a generative AI chatbot learning support tool during upper-elementary media literacy instruction for fake news verification, in contrast to traditional web search and fact-checking websites.

findings.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with 56 upper elementary students (n=28 experimental, n=28 control), the group using Microsoft Copilot significantly improved fake-news recognition from pretest to posttest (M=55.00 to 87.50, t(27)=6.53, p<0.001). After controlling for prior knowledge, the experimental group outperformed the control group on posttest achievement (adjusted M=87.661 vs. 65.196, F(1,53)=29.933, p<0.001).
findings.measure: Fake news recognition test / learning achievement posttest

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI chatbot used for conversational, language-based assistance and response generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a student-facing generative AI chatbot in elementary media literacy instruction, with Microsoft Copilot named as the specific implementation in the paper text.

findings.finding_summary: The experimental group using the generative AI chatbot showed significantly higher fake-news detection learning outcomes than the control group using the Taiwan FactCheck Center website and Google search. Posttest performance was higher after adjusting for pretest scores (adjusted M=87.661 vs. 65.196; F(1,53)=29.933, p<0.001), while the control group's gain was not statistically significant (t(27)=0.983, p=0.334).

Perceived cognitive load was not significantly different between groups. For mental load, the experimental group had M=2.76 and the control group M=3.00, t(54)=-0.523, p=0.603; for mental effort, the experimental group had M=2.80 and the control group M=3.40, t(54)=-1.263, p=0.212.
findings.measure: Cognitive load questionnaire (mental load, mental effort)

findings.finding_summary: Students in the experimental group reported favorable acceptance of the generative AI chatbot. Mean ratings were 4.16 for perceived usefulness and 4.23 for perceived ease of use on a five-point Likert scale, indicating generally positive user perceptions.
findings.measure: Technology acceptance questionnaire (perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with a non-AI control group and clear outcome measures, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and uses a relatively small sample from one school. The design is credible but has moderate risk of bias and limited generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The main academic outcome shows a large and statistically significant advantage for the AI-assisted group, with a substantial posttest gap after covariate adjustment. Although effect sizes were not reported, the reported F statistic and mean difference indicate medium-to-large practical impact.
